neighbours.label: 'in' + patient or population group in clinical caution notes ("avoid in patients … and in …"); weaker on a byline name after 'By'
fire: This medicine should be avoided in patients with severe liver impairment and in nursing mothers.
Dose reduction is advised in patients over seventy and in those with low body weight.
The vaccine is contraindicated in infants under six months and in people with egg allergy.
Caution is needed in children with asthma or in adults taking beta blockers.
Safety has not been established in pregnant women or in adolescents under sixteen.
The cream is not recommended in patients with broken skin or in babies.
Monitor blood pressure closely in patients receiving diuretics and in the frail elderly.
Side effects are more frequent in women taking oral contraceptives and in smokers.
quiet: This medicine should be stored below 25 degrees and kept away from direct sunlight.
Dose reduction is advised when the tablets are taken together with grapefruit juice.
The vaccine is shipped frozen and must be thawed before the nurse prepares it.
Caution is needed when driving, because the tablets can make you drowsy.
Safety data were collected by the manufacturer over a period of ten years.
The cream is applied twice daily to clean, dry skin after washing.
Doctors monitor blood pressure closely for the first week of treatment.
Side effects usually fade after a few days and rarely require treatment.

notes: Card top examples were bylines (By Steve …) plus 'Avoid in patients'. Probes: medical 'in <group>' 0.36-0.47, bylines 0.24-0.28, 'given to patients' 0.15. Test covers the clinical context only.
